candidates.attacker_control: A user who can author or edit wiki content controls both the body of the raw macro and its mandatory syntax parameter. Choosing an HTML-family syntax causes the renderer to treat the body as raw HTML.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The raw macro is explicitly documented as emitting content unchanged, so this is not a bug in trusted contexts. RawBlock is only emitted by the reviewed XHTML renderer for HTML-family syntaxes, which the attacker can select. I found no filter or sanitizer applied to RawBlock before rendering and no restricted-mode check in RawMacro. The HTML macro provides a direct contrast: it rejects clean=false in restricted contexts and configures restricted cleaning, showing that restricted rendering is intended to constrain raw HTML. The search covered the macro implementation, RawBlock, the XHTML renderer, and the restricted-context APIs.
candidates.impact: Stored cross-site scripting and arbitrary HTML injection in pages rendered from untrusted wiki content. Script executes in the victim's origin and can perform actions as the victim or modify page content; the exact account/session impact depends on the host application's deployment and authorization model.
candidates.prerequisites: The raw macro component must be installed/available to the untrusted author, the document must be rendered to an HTML/XHTML target, and the application must use restricted rendering (or otherwise rely on the HTML cleaner / disabled HTML macro) as the security boundary for untrusted content. In a trusted rendering context, raw output is the macro's intended behavior and is not a vulnerability.
candidates.root_cause: RawMacro.execute() constructs a RawBlock directly from the user-supplied macro content and user-selected syntax without consulting MacroTransformationContext.getTransformationContext().isRestricted(). XHTMLChainingRenderer.onRawText() then writes any RawBlock whose syntax is in the HTML family directly through printRaw(), bypassing XML/HTML escaping. The HTML macro explicitly treats restricted mode as a security boundary and refuses unsanitized clean=false output, but the Raw macro provides an equivalent raw-HTML path with no such check.
candidates.title: Raw macro bypasses restricted rendering and emits unsanitized HTML
candidates.trace: Wiki source -> MacroBlock for the raw macro with an HTML-family syntax parameter -> MacroTransformation executes RawMacro -> new RawBlock(attackerContent, attackerSyntax) -> XDOM traversal invokes onRawText(content, syntax) -> XHTMLChainingRenderer sees an HTML-family SyntaxType and calls XHTMLWikiPrinter.printRaw() -> XMLWikiPrinter writes the content without escaping. No restricted-context rejection or downstream sanitization of RawBlock was found in the visible source.
candidates.unverified: The snapshot does not include XWiki Platform callers or deployment configuration, so it is not proven that the raw macro is exposed to untrusted authors or that restricted=true is used as a sanitization boundary in affected deployments. No runtime rendering or exploit execution was performed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

coverage_summary: The scope reported 749 visible source files with no path/sensitive-name/symlink exclusions and no binary skip evidence. I enumerated the production source across the API, XML, wikimodel, syntax, transformation, macro, legacy, and archetype modules, and inspected the untrusted-content paths around wiki parsing, restricted transformation contexts, macro execution, HTML/Raw macros, XHTML rendering, URL/reference parsing, XML parsing, and the Link Checker. The visible snapshot contained no src/test Java sources; only test configuration/resources were exposed. This was a source review only, not an execution or scanner run.
limitations: No XWiki Platform consumer code or deployment configuration was available, so default macro availability, restricted-mode usage, and any platform-level link/HTML sanitization could not be verified.
No dependency source was available for the HTML cleaner, XML reader factory, or AbstractContextStore, limiting verification of their sanitization, entity-resolution, and context-save semantics.
The source snapshot contains no unit/integration test sources that could corroborate intended restricted-mode behavior.
No code, tests, scanners, or payloads were executed; the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF through the Link Checker transformation's server-side HTTP GET of link targets
rejected_leads.reason: DefaultHTTPChecker does fetch queued URL references without private-address filtering, but checking external links is the module's intended function and no source evidence shows the transformation is enabled for untrusted content or that internal destinations are an unsupported boundary. It is a plausible hardening gap, not the strongest demonstrated candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: javascript: URL scheme accepted through the generic :// URL parser and emitted directly into href
rejected_leads.reason: URLResourceReferenceTypeParser accepts arbitrary schemes followed by :// and the XHTML link renderer puts the reference directly in href, which is XSS-capable in browsers. However the parser comment explicitly allows browser-known unknown protocols, and no host-side scheme policy or proof that platform callers do not filter links is present. This remains a plausible but unverified lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Restricted state lost when DefaultMacroContentParser performs nested transformations
rejected_leads.reason: DefaultMacroContentParser creates new TransformationContext(result, syntax), whose constructor defaults restricted to false, so nested macro execution can lose the parent restriction. The in-repository caller that requests transformation is the CTS data macro and actual platform macro call paths are not visible, making exploitability less direct than the Raw macro path.

rejected_leads.lead: RenderingContextStore does not explicitly save the restricted flag before async context restoration
rejected_leads.reason: The store lists PROP_RESTRICTED and restores it but its save override visibly serializes only the syntax entries. The external AbstractContextStore contract and actual async call paths are unavailable, so I could not establish whether the base class saves the flag automatically or whether this is a real lost-restriction bug.

summary: The strongest source-supported issue is a restricted-rendering bypass in the Raw macro. The macro accepts attacker-controlled content and an attacker-selected syntax, wraps them in a RawBlock, and the XHTML renderer writes HTML-family RawBlocks verbatim. Unlike the HTML macro, the Raw macro never checks the restricted transformation context, so content that is supposed to be sanitized for untrusted authors can be emitted as unsanitized HTML/JavaScript. Deployment defaults and the platform caller's use of restricted mode could not be verified from this snapshot, so this remains a candidate rather than a confirmed vulnerability.
